title: Launching Your Course with Canvas
description:
Facilitators: Carlos Perez, Center for Teaching Excellence

Description:
Canvas is more than a place to share course materials; it is a learning environment that students experience outside the classroom. The design of a course in Canvas influences how easily students navigate content, engage with learning activities, complete assignments, and access feedback.

In this session, participants will explore strategies to create a clear, consistent, and accessible Canvas course. These strategies reduce students’ cognitive load; communicate expectations; and support student success from the first day of class.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1) Describe how the design of a Canvas course influences student learning and engagement.

2) Organize course materials using a consistent module structure.

3) Identify opportunities to enhance accessibility and student navigation in Canvas.

title: Preparing for an AAALAC Site Visit
description:
Facilitators: Dr. Jennifer Singleton, Research Compliance Administrator for Education and Outreach, Animal Welfare Office



Description: This session will discuss the upcoming AAALAC International site visit to Texas A&M’s main and Kingsville campuses in early 2027. It will be outlining AAALAC’s role in promoting humane, responsible animal care through triennial accreditation.

Faculty will learn practical preparation steps including reviewing AUPs, eliminating protocol drift, ensuring accurate labeling and recordkeeping, and confirming personnel training requirements. The Animal Welfare Office will provide ongoing guidance through training, communications, and preparatory visits, ensuring attendees know what to expect and how to navigate the lead up to the site visit.


Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1)  AAALAC purpose — Understand AAALAC’s accreditation process and the significance of the 2027 site visit.

2) Preparation expectations — Recognize key preparation steps, including AUP review, protocol drift correction, and required documentation and training.

3) Support and guidance – Identify available guidance, preparatory materials and support contacts.

title: Strained at the Strait: Small Passages, Global Consequences
description:
Memorial Student Center (MSC), Room 2401

The MSC Wiley Lecture Series presents “Strained at the Strait: Small Passages, Global Consequences,” a discussion examining how strategic waterways and geographic chokepoints shape international relations, security, and global trade. Recent developments in the Persian Gulf, South China Sea, Suez Canal, and Panama Canal demonstrate how events in these narrow waterways can have far-reaching global consequences. Disruptions to these routes can delay the movement of goods, raise energy prices, strain international supply chains, and increase the risk of military confrontation. Featuring experts in international affairs, security policy, and maritime strategy, the panel will examine why these waterways matter, how competition over them shapes global politics, and what those developments could mean for our interconnected world.

title: Preparing for the Transition to Huron IACUC
description:
Facilitators: Dr. Jennifer Singleton, Research Compliance Administrator for Education and Outreach, Animal Welfare Office

Description: This session introduces Texas A&M’s transition to the Huron IACUC protocol management system, expected to launch in late Fall/early Spring FY27. New faculty will learn why Huron is replacing iRIS, how its clearer structure, real time transparency, and streamlined workflows will support compliant, efficient research, and what investigators can expect during the transition.

The session will also note the role of a faculty advisory group providing input during implementation, as well as upcoming training resources designed to ensure a smooth, predictable move to the new system.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1) Huron transition overview — Understand the purpose of Texas A&M’s move to Huron IACUC and key benefits for research activities.

2) Implementation expectations — Recognize major FY27 transition milestones and what investigators should prepare for as protocols shift from iRIS.

3) Training and support — Identify available guidance, training tools, and support contacts during system adoption, including input channels such as the faculty advisory group.

title: Conversation Circle for English Language Proficiency
description:
Facilitator: Hayden Lohman, Center for Teaching Excellence

Description: Conversation Circle is a supportive space for practicing spoken English through group discussions on cultural topics, including American university culture. Participants improve spontaneous speaking, active listening, and conversational turn-taking.

Through communication with speakers from a variety backgrounds, they acclimate to different accents. The sessions promote social connections, intercultural dialogue, and a sense of belonging.

The goal is to enhance English fluency, comprehension, and confidence.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to:

1. Employ effective spontaneous communication skills in social, academic and professional settings.
2. Elaborate on their viewpoints and opinions in group discussions.
3. Construct clear and well-structured responses during impromptu conversations.
4. Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions

title: Rethinking Classroom Assessment Techniques
description:
Facilitators: Jean Layne, Center for Teaching Excellence

Carlos Perez, Center for Teaching Excellence

Description:

Whether you teach a large-enrollment lecture, a small seminar, or a fully asynchronous online class, one challenge remains universal: How do you know what your students are learning before high-stakes exams or major assignments?

In this workshop, you will explore the latest edition of Classroom Assessment Techniques (CATs), an updated classic that provides a modern framework for designing real-time, low-stakes assessments across all teaching modalities while addressing the opportunities and challenges of today’s AI-influenced educational landscape. Participants will examine the different categories of CATs and learn how to select and adapt strategies that align with specific learning outcomes.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1) Identify appropriate Classroom Assessment Techniques that align with specific course learning outcomes.

2) Use the Course Learning Outcomes Inventory (CLOI) to identify essential course knowledge and skills and align them with low-stakes assessments.

3) Develop a plan for a Classroom Assessment Technique that can be used in an upcoming class session.

title: Stop Refereeing Group Projects: A Plug-and-Play Toolkit for Student Self-Managing Teams
description:
Facilitators: Nate Poling, Center for Teaching Excellence

Description:
This workshop explores how to design and facilitate small group projects that empower students to manage their own team dynamics, workflows, and internal conflicts. Moving beyond generic project guidelines, participants will examine evidence-based strategies to help student teams self-diagnose and self-correct using vetted, classroom-ready working style inventories and peer charters. We will address common pain points—such as free-riders, communication breakdowns, and grading friction—by introducing modular, just-in-time tools that can be deployed immediately to course-correct current groups or archived to launch seamless collaboration next semester.

Faculty will walk away with access to a pre-organized digital toolkit containing plug-and-play communication templates, workflow matrices, and student-led escalation protocols designed to shift the instructor’s role from group referee to strategic consultant.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1) Design student peer charters and escalation/deescalation protocols to reduce instructor conflict management.

By auditing the assignments and activities you already use, we will explore how small, intentional design tweaks can boost student engagement, success, and retention. Whether you teach a large lecture or a small seminar, this session offers a universal framework to elevate your teaching practices without inflating your grading workload. This foundational overview aligns with institutional goals while connecting you directly to customized CTE consultation support.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to…

1) Modify one existing course assignment to increase student engagement without increasing their grading workload.
